svg.text: temporal.WithTokenProvider is a Go server option, not a config key — which is why this stack compiles its own server binary.
Returns a nil provider, and main.go omits the option
entirely. Passing a nil-valued concrete type would still
look non-nil to the server and break every outbound RPC.
temporal/fx.go refuses to start rather than replicate insecurely:
"…require is true but no TokenProvider is
provider set, but no remote-cluster TLS
A stock temporalio/server image therefore fails fast here.
The provider is now held by RPCFactory, which builds every
connection this cluster opens to a remote cluster.
Keyed by the peer's host name — not its cluster name.
rootCaFiles present ⇒ TLS enabled for this remote
On every single RPC. TokenCredentials caches nothing —
the provider owns the whole token lifecycle.
now < expires − refreshSkew → return the cached token
Wait on it, then re-check — replication opens many streams
at once, and this collapses them into one token request.
expires_in missing or ≤ 0 → assume 1 minute: the worst case
is an extra token request, not a rejected RPC.
The RPC is failed rather than sent bare:
temporal-replication — a service account, no user behind it.
Returns an access token carrying the one claim that matters:
temporal-system is the reserved cluster-wide scope
Anything less and the peer accepts the connection, validates the
signature, then denies every replication call — a silent stall.
public frontend :7233 — the only listener that reads tokens
Verifies the signature against Keycloak's JWKS,
It hardcodes a claim mapper that grants system admin to every
caller — a JWT there would be decorative, never checked.
Every claim above is taken from go.temporal.io/server v1.32.0-160.1 (common/rpc/auth, common/rpc/rpc.go, temporal/fx.go) and server/tokenprovider.go.
